=== WHAT I CONCLUDED AND ON WHAT EVIDENCE ===
1. The fixpoint is data-parallel by construction — each state's new value depends only on previous-sweep children values. Jacobi iteration (read from previous, write to new array) is order-independent and deterministic regardless of thread count.

2. Prior art in retro.zig (B31) uses std.Thread.spawn with worker-on-calling-thread pattern. Adopted this pattern for Jacobi workers. The per-thread-output-and-merge approach is not needed — Jacobi workers write to disjoint ranges of a shared output array.

3. Per-thread memory: ~198 MB extra (L_next + H_next). Peak RSS expected ~3.4 GB with 4 threads vs 3.2 GB serial — within 4 GB cap.

4. Zig 0.16 API changes: std.process.argsAlloc is gone; used std.process.Init.Minimal with init.args.vector. std.time.sleep is gone; used std.Thread.yield().

5. All 384 tests pass, including 4 new T312 race-control tests. Seeded defect positive control catches missing join barrier reliably (10M-element array, main thread does 100 elements, spawned threads do ~3.3M each, check before join finds sentinel values).
